summary: Well-executed, preregistered paired confirmatory study with complete artifact accounting; runs and analysis follow the preregistration and produce a degenerate (ceiling) confirmatory outcome because all shared initial candidates produced no emulator faults. Main remaining defect is an overly verbose Disclosure Statement containing run-level path/hash material that must be condensed to the mandated concise form.
critical_issues: Disclosure Statement still contains run-level file paths and per-file SHA‑256 hashes (e.g., explicit provenance/master_prompt.txt path and hash) and duplicates execution-log provenance; this violates the track’s concise‑disclosure requirement and must be corrected before finalisation.
required_revisions: Condense the Disclosure Statement into a single concise paragraph (within the five-page manuscript) that reports only the mandatory items: LLM(s) used and model identifiers (e.g., gpt-5-mini), orchestration/adapter framework (hosted_netops_gvr_v1), canonical verifier identifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), existence of the preregistration (study id c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001), that execution and analysis artifacts/manifests are archived (name the execution manifest or bundle), provide at most one manifest‑level checksum (not per-file hashes), describe the autonomy-lock boundary (human selected topic and approved initial master prompt pre-lock; autonomous post-lock execution/analysis/manuscript generation), and explicitly state that no human manually edited the manuscript after the autonomy lock. Remove all run-level file paths and per‑file SHA‑256 hashes from the Disclosure prose; refer readers to the archived manifest for low‑level provenance and give at most one manifest-level checksum.
optional_revisions: Add one brief sentence in Methods clarifying that model_configuration.json records temperature = null and that null indicates provider-default sampling semantics (not evidence of deterministic sampling).

If space permits, add a short paragraph in Discussion contrasting how an independent-generation arm or a repair-enabled arm would change the estimand and enable non-degenerate inference, citing the archived sensitivity artifacts.
